competitors.title: LangGraph vs Microsoft Agent Framework: The Real Difference Is State
key_points: Both frameworks now offer graph-based workflows, typed nodes/edges, checkpointing, HITL interruption, multi-agent orchestration, and MCP tool support — feature tables are nearly identical
The real difference is the state contract: LangGraph requires a typed state schema before any code runs (schema-first), while MAF lets you discover state as you build (behavior-first)
LangGraph uses interrupt() to serialize state at the exact pause point and resume from checkpoint; MAF uses an emit-and-rerun model that re-runs the workflow from the current position

LangGraph's learning cost concentrates at the start (4 core concepts: state schema/reducers, compiled graph, checkpointer/thread IDs, conditional edges); MAF's distributes — simple agents are easy, but complex composition hits harder later
LangGraph has larger open-source community and more verified production deployments at scale; MAF is backed by Microsoft with Azure AI Foundry integration and enterprise procurement support
Recommendation: schema-first developers choose LangGraph, behavior-first developers choose MAF; ecosystem considerations are secondary to architectural fit

competitors.title: AI Agent Frameworks Comparison 2026: Complete Guide
key_points: Six production-viable frameworks in 2026: LangChain/LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK, Anthropic Agent SDK, and Mastra
LangGraph is the only Tier 1 production-proven framework with LangSmith monitoring, LangServe deployment, and LangGraph Cloud
LangGraph: 90K+ GitHub stars, Python/TypeScript, graph-based state machines, excellent multi-agent, steep learning curve, best for complex custom workflows and enterprise systems
Microsoft Agent Framework (via Semantic Kernel) listed as Tier 2 production-capable alongside CrewAI and AutoGen AG2
Common mistakes: choosing based on hype, over-engineering the first agent, ignoring maintenance cost, not building a framework abstraction layer, assuming one framework for everything
Framework composition across different system layers is a valid and often optimal architecture pattern

competitors.title: Mastra vs LangGraph vs Microsoft Agent Framework 2026
key_points: LangGraph: 12K+ GitHub stars, Python-only, most mature production deployments, best-in-class HITL workflows, huge ecosystem with every major LLM/tool/vector DB integration
Microsoft Agent Framework: 8K+ GitHub stars (growing fast), Python + .NET, released late 2025, borrows LangGraph's graph model with cleaner APIs, Azure AI Foundry integration
MAF strengths: Semantic Kernel compatibility, enterprise features built-in (RBAC, audit logs, Azure AD), free SOC 2/ISO via Azure hosting
LangGraph weaknesses: Python only, steeper learning curve, LangChain overhead/verbosity, memory management requires deliberate configuration
MAF weaknesses: newest framework with smallest community, best experience requires Azure (vendor pull), fewer third-party integrations than LangChain
2026 reality: LangGraph owns complex Python enterprise tier, MAF is the new Azure default

competitors.title: Microsoft Agent Framework vs LangGraph - AIchitect
key_points: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 (April 2026) is the official merger of AutoGen and Semantic Kernel into a single production-ready SDK for .NET and Python
Choose MAF when: migrating off AutoGen or Semantic Kernel, building .NET-native agents, wanting Microsoft-backed enterprise support
Choose LangGraph when: needing stateful graph-based agent control flow, complex branching/retry logic, production agents needing observability
LangGraph has 28 shared connections (CrewAI, Cursor, LangSmith, LiteLLM, LlamaIndex, etc.) vs MAF's smaller ecosystem
